title: Turn one optimisation pass off for the function

rewrite.template:
#pragma push
#pragma opt_common_subs off   /* or opt_lifetimes / opt_propagation / opt_dead_assignments off */
<fn>
#pragma pop
rewrite.description: Most frequent single fix. opt_common_subs off first, then opt_lifetimes, opt_propagation, opt_dead_assignments. Not allowed in onmokoworks' worker output.

tool: python3 -I tools/pragmasweep.py fn UNIT FN --set all [--objdiff]

tool: python3 -I tools/pragmasweep.py fn UNIT FN (sweeps compilers)

unsigned char al = (int)(255.0f * a);
SetColor(0xFFFFFF00 | al);   /* TU on GC/2.6 */
rewrite.description: Every matched fn with this shape and rN != r0 is in a GC/2.x TU. A 1.3.2 TU faking it with __rlwimi colours the constant r0.

rewrite.template: (solver output)

title: A compiler temp must be numbered next to a local: give the value a named local

rewrite.template:
T tN = <expr>;   /* declared where the solver says */
... tN ...
rewrite.description: The default realisation of a regfix 'renumber temp X next to local Y' diagnosis. Read the value one statement earlier or later if a plain hoist does nothing.

tool: python3 -I tools/shapesweep.py UNIT FN --moves hoist,unvar  then regfix solve

title: Call result through an inline `return f(...)` takes the wrong dying saved reg: name the result in the inline

rewrite.template: static inline int *F(...) { int a; int *ret; int b; ...; ret = Call(...); return ret; }
rewrite.description: Sweep the named result's declaration position among the variables that die at the call (n+1 compiles).

title: Stop an inline from modifying its parameter and returning it; return the expression

rewrite.template:
static inline int F(int chute, int index) { return chute == 2 ? index + 2 : index; }
/* not: if (chute == 2) index += 2; return index; */
rewrite.description: A parameter that is reassigned inside the inline becomes an extra temp. Returning an expression removes it.

title: Advance a cursor through an inline in/out parameter

rewrite.template:
static inline void Next(void ***cursor) { ... (*cursor)++; }
/* then index = byte offset / sizeof(void *) */
rewrite.description: A walker that the target keeps in a separate register from the base: route it through a pointer-to-cursor inline.

title: Compute an element address only where it is used; drop manual pointer increments

rewrite.template: if (cond) { Face *face = &faces[count]; ... }   /* no out++ / p += size walkers */
rewrite.description: Fewer strength-reduced pointers means fewer hidden temps competing for the target's registers.

title: Index through the full expression instead of a cached pointer

rewrite.template: grid->cells[index].tris   /* not: Cell *c = &grid->cells[index]; c->tris */
rewrite.description: The inverse of temp-to-local: a named pointer forces an extra live range the target does not have.

title: Write repeated per-point code as a small local array plus a counted loop (fully unrolled by MWCC)

rewrite.template:
Vec3f control[3] = {a, b, c};
for (i = 0; i < 3; i++) { ... control[i] ... }
rewrite.description: An unrolled loop gets different temps from three written-out copies; the scratch registers match the target's.

title: Initialise the counter in the caller and pass its address to the inline

rewrite.template:
int n = 0;
Fill(&n, ...);   /* inline increments *n */
rewrite.description: Moves the zero constant and the counter into the caller's numbering.

title: Replace a C++ implicit member copy with a memberwise C static inline

rewrite.description: Implicit operator= has its own load/store order and also changes function emission order.

title: Match the declaration to the real definition (drop a wrong const, fix the element type)

rewrite.template: extern int lbl_804EC5E8[65];   /* the shared header had const */
rewrite.description: const lets MWCC hoist loads over stores (GC/2.6) and CSE them; a mismatch changes schedule and registers.

title: Change only the integer type of a local (int / long / unsigned)

rewrite.template: long clamp;   /* was int */
rewrite.description: int, long and unsigned int are different IR types: the register can move with identical instructions.

title: Rewrite the loop's index arithmetic (p=&a[i] / p++ / base+i*size, shared or scoped counters)

rewrite.template: x = 0x3C + g*0xBB;  /* position from the index, not a running counter */
rewrite.description: Strength reduction creates hidden IVs. Try all of: computed position, p++, &a[i], one shared function-scope i, a scoped counter per loop.

title: Move a loop (or one of several identical blocks) into a static inline helper

rewrite.template: static inline void Fill(T *p, int n) { int i; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) ... }
rewrite.description: An inlined body gets its own temps and a deeper priority; changes the SR init (`mr`) and which dying reg a walker reuses. If only one of several identical blocks differs, some were inline expansions.

title: A caller local reused by several switch cases is numbered below the loop temps: give each case an inline helper with its own local

rewrite.template:
static inline void CreateX(const char *name) { Menu *m = Create(name, 1); if (m != 0) { for (int i = 0; ...) Add(m, tbl[i]); } }
/* case 0: CreateX(s + 0x5d8); break;   instead of: menu = Create(...); if (menu) ...; */
rewrite.description: regfix diag says 'X is a named local, numbered below every temp: turn it into a temp'. A function-scope local shared by several cases cannot be renumbered by decl order; moving each case body (create + null check + loop) into its own static inline turns it into an inline local with a fresh number. Then re-run the decl-order step for the remaining named locals (a block-scoped loop variable moved to function scope).

title: An inline's local must be numbered above a temp created earlier: declare it in the outer inline/caller and pass it by reference

rewrite.template:
static inline void Inner(T *self, const char *file, unsigned long &size) { if (file) { size = ...; ... } }
static inline void Outer(...) { const char *file; unsigned long size; ...; Inner(self, file, size); }
rewrite.description: regfix diag 'create temp @B (an inline local) after temp @A (an earlier inline param/local)' = @B needs a lower @ number than it gets, i.e. it must be created earlier in the frontend. Declaring the variable one inline level up (after the variable it must follow) and passing it by reference does that; the reference is folded away. Sweep its position among the outer inline's locals.

title: Target keeps &local in a saved GPR across a loop: declare before the loop and pass via a pointer variable

rewrite.description: Moving the declaration alone does nothing; a pointer local inside an inline is propagated away.

title: List iterator kept in a stack slot: derived iterator class passed by value to an inline

rewrite.description: Plain iterator classes are always registerised; a trivial dtor also does it but adds extab.

title: Reorder independent statements

rewrite.template: (stmtsweep output)
rewrite.description: Statement order changes vreg creation order and the scheduler's input; R5 bc31b3a, TextRenderer_DrawEntry 783ff7e.

title: Change expression form: component/store order, operand order, assignment inside a call arg

rewrite.template:
out->y = ...; out->z = ...; out->x = ...;   /* target store order */
f(y = 300 - 4*a);   /* temp assigned inside the call arg */
rewrite.description: Changes the expression DAG, not the variables. Call args are evaluated right to left.

title: Use float literals instead of `extern const float lbl_...`

rewrite.template: x = 1.0f;   /* not lbl_806D28CC */
rewrite.description: Literals can be CSE'd and hoisted, extern consts are memory loads. postprocess_sdata2 maps @N back to lbl_ names.

title: Vector x 4x4 matrix with translation: inner products parenthesised, translation as the outer left operand

rewrite.template:
float y = v->y; float x = v->x; float z = v->z;
out->x = m[3][0] + (z*m[2][0] + (x*m[0][0] + y*m[1][0]));
rewrite.description: Exact in Mtx44_TransformVec3 (GC/1.3.2 C). fn_8019EB9C (GC/2.6 C++, out may equal v) matched with left-assoc sums `m[0][0]*vx + vy*m[1][0] + vz*m[2][0] + m[3][0]` stored straight to out, and __restrict on the matrix and input pointers (rule restrict-input-ptrs).

title: Load scheduled above a store: read through a const pointee (GC/2.6) or __restrict

rewrite.template: const T *self;   /* or float (*__restrict src)[4] */
rewrite.description: GC/2.6 hoists loads over stores only from const sources; 1.3.2 never does. __restrict reproduces software-pipelined copies. If __restrict on self fixes one hoist but also hoists a self-> load over a store to a global that the target keeps in order, drop __restrict and declare the hoisted global `extern const` instead (fn_8024AD8C).

title: Long copy run: regroup statements so the 26-statement scheduling region breaks where the target's does

rewrite.template: dst->blk = src->blk;   /* one 16-byte struct copy instead of 4 statements */
rewrite.description: Count statements from the block start; merge/split statements to move the break.

title: Value in r0 but target uses r4..r7: route a nearby load through that value

rewrite.template: LNode **a = &l->f4; e.n = (LNode *)a; b.n = a[1];   /* not e.n = &l->f4; b.n = l->head; */
rewrite.description: r0 can't be a load base; once the value is used as a base it skips r0.

title: Chained `a = b = 0` gives the zero the counter's register

rewrite.template: p->n = j = 0;   /* fakematch if not natural */
rewrite.description: Fakematch rule applies: mark with the natural code.

title: Extra lis/addi or missing `addi rX, rBase, 0`: the TU must own the pooled data (not a source-shape fix)

rewrite.template: splits.txt: .rodata/.data start..end on the TU; define the objects as real statics in source order
rewrite.description: Anchor needs >=3 compiler-local objects; named globals never. A static object behind the anchor gives 'first access folded, rest through a pointer'.

title: Local lifetimes: lexical blocks, reuse one variable, split or merge locals

rewrite.template: { int t; ... }   /* scope a local to its block, or reuse dy for the next value */
rewrite.description: Group 'Local lifetimes / lexical blocks / variable reuse' of the onmokoworks Codex fixes.

title: Move the function boundary: add, remove or reshape an inline helper

rewrite.template: static inline T Helper(...) { ... }
rewrite.description: Group 'Inline helper / function boundary' of the onmokoworks Codex fixes (36, the largest).

title: Literal vs extern constant (int or float)

rewrite.template: 1.0f / 0x10   vs   extern const float lbl_...
rewrite.description: Group 'Literal vs extern constant' of the onmokoworks Codex fixes.

title: Part of the function is the body of an already-matched function: the original inlined it

rewrite.template: static inline void Helper(T *c, ...) { <verbatim body of the matched sibling> }
rewrite.description: Run `tools/asmgrep.py similar UNIT FN` (or grep the TU's distinctive globals/strings in src/) and look for a MATCHED function whose whole body appears as a run inside the near miss. Copy that body verbatim as a static inline and call it. The sibling's named locals become inline temps, which are numbered above the caller's locals and so are coloured earlier: this is the usual realisation of the regfix diagnosis "named local X must be numbered above temp Y". Values the caller already holds in a saved register (a string base) go in as parameters.

auto: regfix fix: moves `inline[plain|argdecl] NAME: stmts i..j` (extract the run holding a diagnosed local's live range into a static inline) + `boolnorm` (x = a != 0 <-> a ? 1 : 0, also inside the helper). Replays fn_8024D3D4 (needs both). Not covered: b27f188 (by-value iterator type), eb9631d (macros->inlines + __restrict).

title: Unrolled run of stores in the target, but ours keeps a pointer CSE'd across it: write the run as a loop

rewrite.description: The target re-loads a pointer (e.g. lwz r3, 0x20(rSelf)) at the start of an unrolled run of stores that ours takes from a register still live from an earlier read of the same field (our extra use moves the earlier temp to another register). MWCC unrolls small constant loops in the backend, after frontend CSE, so the original wrote the run as a loop; hand-unrolled stores get CSE'd with the earlier read.

title: Local must be coloured right before a later inline's temps: compute it through a nested (level-2) inline

rewrite.description: MWCC expands inlines level by level (all direct calls first, in statement order, then their callees). A named local is coloured after every temp; a level-1 inline puts it before all later level-1 inlines' temps. Wrapping it two levels deep creates its temps after the level-1 inlines' locals but before loop-opt temps.

tool: python3 -I tools/regfix.py diag UNIT FN  (look for 'X is a named local ... turn it into a temp' with the wanted spot between later temps)

title: Loop unrolled 4x in the target but 8x in ours (or not the same scheme): up-counting loop + #pragma opt_unroll_instr_count 16

rewrite.template:
#pragma push
#pragma opt_unroll_instr_count 16
... fn ...
#pragma pop
/* loop: for (u32 i = 0; i < n; i++) { *dst++ = ...; p += 2; } */
rewrite.description: An unsigned count-down loop (for (; n > 0; n--)) gets the 4x srwi./andi. unroll but its guard is simplified to beq; the up-counting i < n loop gives the target's cmplwi/ble guard but MWCC unrolls it 8x. Lowering the unroll budget (opt_unroll_instr_count 16, GC/1.3.2) brings the up-counting loop to the target's 4x shape. Also when a manually unrolled loop keeps constants (li) inside the loop but the target hoists them: backend LICM (CodeMotion.c maymove) refuses to move a PC_LI when loop->bodySize > 25, so the target's source loop was the small rolled one, unrolled later by the compiler (fn_80293070).

title: Target copies a value into a loop register with `mr` (or keeps a separate trip-count temp) where ours coalesces: make the loop variable a named local of the real function

rewrite.template:
static inline int Receive(Card *c, int &i) { ... for (i = len - 1; i > 0; i--) ... }
extern "C" void Tick(Card *card) { int i; ... r = card->Receive(i); }
rewrite.description: MWCC coalesces a copy whose destination is an inline temp (inline param/local), but keeps the copy when the destination is a named local of the function being compiled. A target `mr rA,rB` at a loop entry (pointer copy before a send loop, `subic. r0; mr r3,r0` before an unrolled loop) therefore means the loop variable was a function-level local: declare it in the real function and pass it into the inline by reference. The opposite also holds: inline-local loop counters give `li rA,0; mr rB,rA` counter/offset pairs, function-level counters two `li`.

tool: hand; python3 -I tools/regfix.py diag UNIT FN

title: Hand-expanded recursion: write the recursive functions and set #pragma inline_depth (+ -inline deferred)

rewrite.description: Auto-inlining of self/cross recursive calls produces the nested copies; inline_depth sets how many levels; -inline deferred inlines functions defined later and emits functions in reverse source order. Merge the neighbouring TUs that hold the out-of-line copies.

tool: sweep #pragma inline_depth(1..10) and compare bl counts/lengths

title: A named local assigned twice (or from an inline return) loses its named number: one named local per assignment, value written in place, then decl order

rewrite.description: MWCC splits a named local into webs; only the first web keeps the low named-local vreg number, later assignments become frontend temps. When regfix diag wants a temp numbered among the named locals and that temp is a re-assignment of an existing local (or an inline call's value copied into a local, which gets copy-propagated), give it its own named local / write the expression in place, then run the decl-order solver.

tool: hand; python3 -I tools/regfix.py diag UNIT FN; decl-order sweep

title: A constant loaded twice (compare + assign) is CSE'd into a late temp: read it into an inline local before the test

rewrite.template:
float zero = lbl_CONST;
if (zero == d->angle) { dx = zero; ... }
rewrite.description: CSE merges repeated loads of the same global into one temp whose creation number comes after the inline's locals, so it is coloured at the wrong point. When regfix diag asks to swap the creation order of the constant's lfs/lwz temp with an earlier temp, load the constant into a local right before its first use; then fix the remaining local order by decl order.

tool: hand; python3 -I tools/regfix.py diag UNIT FN

title: All loads scheduled before the stores although out may alias the inputs: __restrict on the INPUT pointers (not on out)

when.diag: pre-RA scheduler order differs; loads of the next component wait for the previous store in ours

rewrite.template: void f(const M *__restrict a, Vec3 *out, const Vec3 *__restrict v) { out->x = ...; out->y = ...; out->z = ...; }
rewrite.description: __restrict on out instead leaves the store/load order edges in the scheduler DAG (40 lines); on a and v the DAG loses them and the natural straight-store source matches with no pragma. See regalloc_patterns section 30.

title: A load stuck behind stack stores because the pointer is 'sized array + offset past its end' (Alias.c make_alias gives worst case): address the real object

when.diag: pre-RA scheduler keeps a load after stores to an address-taken local; the pointer is base symbol + offset beyond that symbol's size

rewrite.template: ys = choiceY;            /* not (char *)lbl_base + 0x1dc */
rewrite.description: optimizer/Alias.c make_alias returns NULL (worst case) for offset > object->type->size unless the object is an array of unknown size. Point the pointer at the object that holds the data. See regalloc_patterns section 31.

title: Every access to a data block comes off one base register (section anchor) but ours uses separate lis/addi: merge the over-split TUs into the one that owns the pool

when.diag: target addresses several rodata objects off one anchor register; ours materialises each symbol

rewrite.template: one TU owning the .rodata pool, same compiler for all parts
rewrite.description: The anchor exists only when the objects are defined in the same TU. Merge the neighbours, one compiler, one copy of each prototype, auto_inline off where a now-local callee gets inlined, extab_padding so renames run. See regalloc_patterns section 32.

title: GC/1.2.5 unit: an independent op ahead of the first of two stores through the same pointer cannot be scheduled there (no alias analysis): the block is unscheduled, use #pragma scheduling off and source order

when.diag: GC/1.0-1.2.5n unit; target puts addi/li before a ready store to a pointer that is stored to again later in the block

rewrite.template: #pragma scheduling off  /* + statements in target order; out-of-place adds (q = p + 3) so peephole-forward does not sink them */
rewrite.description: 1.2.5's scheduler orders every pair of pointer accesses (no offsets), so the first store is always higher than the addi. Target = code-generation order. See regalloc_patterns section 33, mwcc_internals 'GC/1.x backend'.

title: One named loop counter shared by many independent loops is a single web: give the loops separate variables

when.diag: mwccdbg: a loop counter vreg coloured first with 'target varies' over several registers

rewrite.template: int i, j; int nameLen, rx0, rx1; /* each loop its own counter */
rewrite.description: MWCC never splits a named local into webs. Greedy: rename one loop's counter at a time, keep those that lower the diff. See regalloc_patterns section 35.

title: Long-lived temp pushed in the 2nd simplify sweep takes a saved reg too early: add named locals (low vreg numbers) in its live range so it is pushed in sweep 1

when.diag: one temp elsewhere gets r27 vs target r28 (or similar), the vreg holding the extra saved reg is coloured early with degree K+1..K+2 and few lower-numbered neighbours

rewrite.template: int row = self->row; int column = self->column; f(row, column);  /* and/or: T *g; g = self->field; use(g); ... g = self->field; */
rewrite.description: Simplify sweeps vregs ascending and repeats; a node from sweep 2 is coloured before all sweep-1 nodes. Named locals get numbers below the temps, so each pushable named neighbour lowers the degree before the temp's sweep-1 turn. See regalloc_patterns section 35.

title: Prologue address constants (base vtable vs body globals) coloured in the wrong order: move the base-class initializer store into the derived ctor body

when.diag: ctor prologue lis/addi pairs with masked symbols differ only in which register holds which symbol; base vtable needs a higher vreg than the body's address locals

rewrite.template: Base() {}  /* no initializer */ ... Derived::Derived() { T *data = ...; *(const void **)this = baseVtable; vtable = data + off; }
rewrite.description: Codegen numbers vregs in order; the base initializer is generated before the body, so its lis gets the lowest number and is coloured last. Storing it in the body after the locals renumbers it. See regalloc_patterns section 36.

title: EH region marker (stw r1, off(rFrame)) placed inside a null-check body: open the try after the check, not around the placement new

when.diag: only the `stw r1, N(r31)` EH marker moves: target emits it inside the `if (q)` body (after its loads), ours before the branch

rewrite.template: T *q = new (p) T; if (q) { try { *q = v; } catch (...) { throw; } }
rewrite.description: The stw r1 that marks the active try region is emitted where the try opens; a try that wraps the null check puts it before the branch. KeyVecBase<KeyGroup>::init fn_801C1964 (11f056f).

title: Int and float call arguments loaded in the wrong order: change the prototype's int/float parameter interleaving (same registers, different evaluation order)

when.diag: only the loads of one call's arguments differ in order, and the swapped pair is an int (rN) and a float (fN) argument

rewrite.template: void f(Obj *n, float t, void *anim, float a); /* was (Obj *, void *, float, float) */
rewrite.description: call_function (FunctionCalls.c) evaluates arguments in parameter order; GPR and FPR numbering is independent, so moving a float parameter before a pointer keeps the registers and changes the schedule. clNormal3D_SetScale is really (obj, frame, anim, ...) (fn_8021ABFC, regalloc_patterns 37).

title: `c ? x : 0` folds to the andc/mask form but the target keeps a branch or a real select: make the zero arm a non-constant

when.diag: ours has neg/andc/and (mask select) where the target has cmp + branch + li 0 (or the reverse), around a ?: with a literal 0 arm

rewrite.template: int zero = 0; ... v = c ? x : zero;  /* optionally #pragma opt_propagation off */
rewrite.description: gen_COND takes the mask path only when one arm is an EINTCONST zero. A zero that reaches the backend as a variable keeps the branch form. Seen as the clFlowCourse Dtor/Update `%2` swap.

title: Saved registers of two locals are swapped and one local is first assigned after an early return: give it a dead def at the top with opt_dead_assignments off

when.census: reg_only or reg+sched swap between callee-saved registers

when.diag: the local whose register is wrong has its first def after an early-out branch

rewrite.template:
#pragma opt_dead_assignments off
T *p; int i; p = 0; if (!enabled) return 0; p = table; ...
rewrite.description: The dead def starts the live range before the early return, so the variable gets its vreg and interference earlier and the colouring order changes. Fakematch: mark it. PCBCheck_ProcessLinks (leversweep). The pragma alone or the dead def alone leaves 4 diff lines.

title: Target keeps a*a + b*b as fmuls/fmuls/fadds while the function fuses elsewhere: multiply through an inline mul(a,b) helper with the operands passed directly

when.census: fmadds in ours vs fmuls+fadds in target, or fp reg/load-order swap at a sum of products

when.diag: other fmadds in the same target function, so fp_contract off is ruled out

rewrite.template:
static inline float mul(float a, float b) { return a * b; }
... sqrtf(mul(d.x, d.x) + mul(d.z, d.z));
rewrite.description: Inline results are temps that do not fuse and get the target numbering. Pass the member expressions directly; named locals or a sq(v) helper stay 3 lines off. fp_contract off around an inline has no effect. JumpDistanceMode_Update.

title: Small table read through a named const object vs an anonymous init blob: use a block-local array initialiser at the use (or the reverse)

when.diag: ours loads table words through a named rodata symbol (or copies a struct from it); the target copies an anonymous blob to the stack inside the block and indexes the stack copy (or the reverse)

rewrite.template: { int arr[5] = {0x16B4, 0x16B3, 0x16B2, 0x16B1, 0x16B0}; for (...) use(arr[i]); }  /* was: static const int arr[5] / FKParams params = lbl_table */
rewrite.description: A local array initialiser emits an anonymous init blob in function order and a stack copy when its block is entered; a struct copy from a named table reads the named object. clFlowKart_UpdateDisplay rank table (5eca6fc).

title: Target has `addi rX,anchor,N` where ours has two addi or a folded displacement: N is the start of a real object; split the pool there and index it directly

when.diag: function uses a section anchor; ours computes base_object + constant (struct-of-pool pointer or Advance-pointer inline), target has a single addi rX,anchor,N followed by index arithmetic

rewrite.template: static float lbl_A[512]; static float lbl_B[384]; ... return &lbl_B[idx];  /* was: (float *)((char *)&pool + 0x98C) + idx via inline */
rewrite.description: MWCC never folds a constant into an anchored object's address, so each distinct addi offset is an object boundary. Split the pool object (source + symbols.txt sizes) at those offsets, type the pieces, convert every pool use in the function (a single named static is not anchored) and write the natural index expression. regalloc_patterns 40.

title: A value built in two steps through a local (end = a + b; ... end - 1): write it as one expression at the use

when.census: reg_only / reg+sched, or add/addi operand order differs

when.diag: a named local is assigned once and read once in straight-line code

rewrite.template: end = file.startAddr + file.length - 1;  /* was: end = start + length; ... f(end - 1) */
rewrite.description: The single expression changes operand association and makes the intermediate a temp instead of a named local. ClSound_InitSoundSystem (0b362350). shapesweep `unvar` does the same on the function body only; leversweep also reaches TU inlines.

title: Target adds a member offset to the index and loads indexed (slwi; addi rI,rI,OFF; lhzx): write (base + index) + OFF with the constant last

when.diag: ours `add rP,rBase,rI; lhz/lfs OFF(rP)`, target `addi rI,rI,OFF; lhzx/lfsx rBase,rI`

rewrite.template: *(unsigned short *)((char *)this + (i + 1) * 2 + 0x28)  /* was name.c[i + 1] */
rewrite.description: Member and array spellings and parenthesised base + (idx + OFF) all give the displacement form; the unparenthesised byte expression with the constant last (or a scalar-array view whose element index carries the offset) gives the indexed form. Fakematch. regalloc_patterns 42.
